SeasonRecapParagraphs: St. Andrew's made Mandy Stinson's first season as head coach a breakthrough year, finishing 19-3 and turning a promising roster into a region champion and state finalist. The Saints were already 3-1 by early September, then found the rhythm that carried them through the heart of the schedule behind senior leadership and a freshman surge from Mary Wilkowski.

Region play became the team's signature. St. Andrew's beat Holly Hill on Sept. 23 and then kept rolling through Beaufort, Colleton Prep, James Island Christian, Charleston Collegiate, and Holly Hill again. By the end of the regular season, the Saints were 10-0 in SCISA Region 2-AA, owned the region title, and had earned the top south seed for the state tournament.

The postseason showed how complete the group had become. Becca Cooper gave St. Andrew's a powerful presence at the net, Carie Bugos steadied the Saints from setter, and Mary Wilkowski kept elevating her play as the stage grew. St. Andrew's beat Greenwood Christian in the state tournament opener, then defeated Calhoun Academy twice in one day to earn a place in the SCISA Class AA championship match.

The season ended at Porter-Gaud School in Charleston against undefeated Pee Dee Academy. St. Andrew's dropped the final 25-19, 25-13, 28-26, but pushed the last set deep and left with a 19-3 record, a 10-0 region championship, and a SCISA AA state runner-up finish that moved the program another step forward after the previous year's semifinal run.

SeasonRecapParagraphs: St. Andrew's entered Mandy Stinson's second season as head coach with a rebuilt lineup and a new offense. The Saints had lost much of the previous year's state runner-up team, but the 2004-05 roster quickly took shape around sophomore Mary Wilkowski, juniors Grace Wilkowski, Maggie Hinchey, Kristen Albritton, Emily Aimone, Caitlin Webb, and Becca Timms, sophomore Courtney Manson and Kim Lucas, and senior Maggie de la Sierra.

The opening month mixed wins with the tougher schedule that later became part of the team's championship story. St. Andrew's started with early victories over Bible Baptist and Providence Christian, with Mary Wilkowski piling up kills and aces and Manson and Albritton handling setting duties. The Saints also absorbed losses to Hilton Head Christian, Thomas Heyward, and Hilton Head Prep while continuing to pick up wins over Bible Baptist, Beaufort Academy, and several recovered-but-unidentified opponents.

By mid-October, the Saints were 9-5 after a non-region loss to Thomas Heyward, then opened SCISA Region 2-AA play with a four-set win over Beaufort Academy behind Grace Wilkowski's 8 kills and Mary Wilkowski's 7 kills, 5 blocks, 4 aces, and 7 digs. Hilton Head Prep beat St. Andrew's five days later, but the season's later coverage credited matches against stronger SCISA Class AAA programs such as Hilton Head Prep and Thomas Heyward with sharpening St. Andrew's for the Class AA field.

The state tournament turned the season. On Oct. 23, St. Andrew's went 5-1 in the double-elimination, eight-team SCISA Class AA tournament, beating Williamsburg Academy, Marlboro Academy, Trinity Collegiate, and W. Wyman King twice after also taking a loss to W. Wyman King. Those back-to-back wins over W. Wyman King in the semifinals sent the Saints to the championship match at the College of Charleston.

St. Andrew's finished the job against Richard Winn Academy on Oct. 27, rallying after a first-set loss to win 19-25, 25-17, 25-13, 25-9 and capture the SCISA Class AA state championship. Mary Wilkowski led the final with 15 kills, 8 blocks, 7 aces, and 8 digs, while Grace Wilkowski added 11 kills, 2 blocks, 11 aces, and 5 digs. Kristen Albritton set the Saints' attack, Mary and Grace combined for 26 kills, and St. Andrew's closed a rebuilding season as state champion at 16-6.

SeasonRecapParagraphs: St. Andrew's turned the 2005-06 season into a near-perfect championship defense, finishing 17-1 under head coach Mandy Stinson and assistant coach Kim Riordan. The Saints opened fast with early wins over Providence Christian, Holly Hill Academy, and Bible Baptist, then proved they could handle pressure with a five-set region win over Hilton Head Christian.

The Saints carried that momentum through the Region 4 race behind the Wilkowski sisters, Megan Hall, Kristen Albritton, Courtney Manson, and a senior group that gave the team balance and leadership. St. Andrew's swept Thomas Heyward and Beaufort, beat Hilton Head Christian again to reach 11-0, and shared the Region 4 crown with Hilton Head Prep after a season that made the defending champions one of Savannah's strongest volleyball teams.

St. Andrew's entered the SCISA Class AA State Tournament as the No. 1 seed in the Upper State Division and played like it. The Saints swept Trinity in Sumter, advanced past Richard Winn Academy, and reached the championship match without dropping a game, setting up a title match with Holly Hill Academy at John Kresse Arena on the College of Charleston campus.

The final was another statement. St. Andrew's beat Holly Hill 25-10, 25-17, 25-12 to win its second consecutive SCISA Class AA championship, with Mary Wilkowski controlling the middle, Grace Wilkowski and Megan Hall sparking runs from the service line, and all four seniors seeing action. The Saints closed the year 17-1, repeating as state champions and sending Grace Wilkowski, Caitlin Webb, Emily Aimone, and Kristen Albritton out with another ring.
